title: Sample 17-18: Word Formation Using Arrows

illustrates.quote: Arrows. Use spaced arrow symbols when print arrows show progression in word formation. List all arrow symbols on the Special Symbols page, or in a transcriber's note before the text.

blocks.text: If the noun ends in ch, s, sh, x, or z
If the noun ends in a consonant + y
Then generally: change y to i and add -es

print.notes: A cell-7 heading, a symbols note (arrow, plus sign), then a two-part table of plural rules (transcribed as running text, not a table, per the given braille's own linearised layout) each with an arrow-formatted word-formation example.
print.printFeatures: A 3-column grid table with column headers in full caps; arrows in the example column.

braille.notes: Byte-identical between A and B; matches independent re-extraction exactly.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille and rule id unchanged ('17.13.2', matches the source's own cross-reference within this rule's own text). Modeled as a linear sequence of paragraphs and lists (not a table block), since the given braille shows NO table/box structure at all — matching precedent's own 'follow the given braille's structure, not the print table's', e.g. buildModel9's displayed-material convention. The all-caps 'IF...THEN GENERALLY...EXAMPLE' column headers are folded into the given braille's own running-sentence wording ('If the noun ends in...', 'Then generally...', 'Example:') rather than modeled as a table header row, since that is what the braille itself already shows the transcriber did.
